body:
sounds good except for 4 - some selectors especially in forms are quite complex and might be hard to convey clearly without actually showing the raw selector.

If we can work around this then we don't need to show them, otherwise we should show the selector.

See how this works out in some mockups: 
https://docs.google.com/document/d/1sYEdRp48kXCofHvisKA9-UOLBRu7mzg8vxG0drY2vg8/edit#heading=h.fltci8lkrw5
BTW I believe we can compute whether a directive is structural or not by looking for  `ViewContainerRef` and `TemplateRef<...>` classes injected into the constructor.

So we could relax the test to whether it injects a `ViewContainerRef` which would pick up `NgComponentOutlet`, `NgTemplateOutlet` and `RouterOutlet`. But I agree that it is not possible to automatically identify `NgSwitch` and `NgPlural` via this approach.

Actually thinking about this some more, I am not sure there is much benefiting in actually labelling a directive as structural. It is something that should be explained in the docs but having a tag (or being able to filter by "structural" type) doesn't seem of much use IMO.
